name: The Operation
overview: In its own best terms the Operation's worldview is that the movement is Trump, and Trump's power is the program. Policies come and go; what lasts is a disciplined political machine that keeps the coalition together (the MAGA base plus the swing voters who returned in 2024), wins elections, and spares the president needless fights. So it runs the campaign through Trump himself, holds the money until it counts (MAGA Inc. held to Labor Day, then about $277M spent by Oct 14), lowers the temperature when the base's demands cost swing seats (quieter raids, no Iran escalation before the vote), and refuses to name an heir. Wiles states it as professionalism: no agenda of her own, only his.

The interest layer: a political machine is also a marketplace for access. Wiles controls Trump's time, so everyone who needs him needs her; an open succession keeps it that way. Blair and LaCivita control the largest pot of money in Republican politics (about $473M raised, 96% from $1M+ donors), and its donors are crypto, energy, AI and casino money with business before the government; several later got posts or pardons for relatives (no causation shown). Their consulting businesses sell Trump-circle proximity abroad: both were paid 'hundreds of thousands' through a law firm retained by Republika Srpska while running Trump's PAC, LaCivita's firm took $1.6M from Albania's opposition, and Wiles's daughter is a partner at a firm that works for Srpska.

Acts depart from words where the business meets the job. Trump called them 'outside consultants' he would 'terminate' if conflicted (Oct 7); the inquiry ended after their fees went to his library (Oct 23), so the remedy was a payment to the principal, not a break with the client. The Operation also loses the fights it says it runs: it wanted quieter raids and the Maximalists got 3,000 arrests a day (Oct 6); Salazar says she warned Blair and Wiles about Latino losses (Oct 31). And its prize asset cannot run again, so the value of controlling access to him starts to decay the day after Nov 3.

Precedent (my reading): Mark Hanna and William McKinley, 1896. A manager raised unprecedented corporate money, set strategy and ran access to the candidate, and his power was the candidate's power. It held while McKinley lived and Hanna kept a Senate seat of his own. It breaks here: Hanna's donors wanted a policy (gold and tariffs) that McKinley also wanted, while the Operation's donors and foreign clients want different things from different parts of government, and its operators hold no office of their own once Trump's term ends.

MID.title: Midterms

paras: What happened.

Blair and LaCivita were each paid “hundreds of thousands” through a Washington law firm retained by the Republika Srpska government to advise Milorad Dodik before the Oct 4, 2026 elections (NYT, via Al Jazeera). Srpska has paid more than $4M to Trump-linked lobbyists and operatives since the start of 2025 (DOJ filings).

The US removed sanctions on Dodik and close associates on Oct 29, 2025 (OFAC). Dodik’s travel ban was reportedly lifted in June at the same time as Berisha’s, the Albanian politician LaCivita worked for before Albania’s 2025 elections. Timing is reported; no source proves the lobbying caused it.

Continental Strategy, where Wiles’s daughter Katie is a partner, has been paid $35,000 a month by Srpska since February (DOJ filings). A Continental partner arranged a September White House meeting between Wiles and a Srpska official; Continental says Katie played no role in it.

Katie Wiles went to Srpska in August with John Calce, a Texas energy executive exploring a gas pipeline with the Srpska government. Calce also runs America First Refining, in which Trump Jr. holds a minority stake; Trump endorsed its Brownsville refinery in March, and the company and a predecessor paid Continental $750,000 to lobby the White House and Energy Department (NYT, via DNyuz).

Oct 7: Trump called Blair and LaCivita “outside consultants” and said he would fire them if there was a conflict; he later said there was none. Bannon called them grifters and demanded a review of the money.
Why it is a blunder for the faction. It hands Bannon a weapon and arms the Maximalists. The Operation’s own interest cannot explain it.
Who and why.

Blair Motives: (1) Money: each fee is a payday on top of his MAGA Inc. role. (2) Selling proximity: a Bosnian editor told Al Jazeera the main benefit for Dodik was closeness to Trump, which is a product Blair can only sell while he is in Trump’s inner circle (reported). (3) Exposure: he accepted the risk anyway, which suggests he judged Trump would not punish it.
LaCivita Motives: same as Blair, with a second foreign client, Berisha, who also received travel-ban relief in the same period (reported timing).

Wiles did not take the fees herself. Motives: (1) Family business: her daughter’s firm earns from the same client, so criticizing the operators would expose her family. (2) Access as an asset: the firm’s other client, America First Refining, has Trump Jr. as an investor and a Trump-endorsed project (documented). No source shows Wiles acted on any of it.

Oct 22-23: both gave their Srpska fee (believed over $100,000 each) to Trump's presidential library; LaCivita called it 'an honor and a no brainer', and Trump said his inquiry was over (Daily Beast, citing NY Post). The remedy was a payment to the principal, not an end to the foreign work (my reading).

paras: Position.
No heir named. Trump says he has “never talked about it” (Oct 20).
MAGA Inc., the largest pot of campaign money, stays under Blair and LaCivita.
Why the faction does it. An open race keeps every contender dependent on the people who control Trump’s access and his campaign money.
Who and why.

Wiles keeps the question open. Motives: (1) Power: the chief of staff controls access to Trump, and she already has to manage people who do not need her for it, including Trump’s children, Kushner and Musk (AP). A named heir would add another center that does not run through her (my reading). (2) Job security: a named heir makes Trump a lame duck, and her authority is borrowed from his.

Blair, LaCivita hold the money. Motives: (1) Leverage: the money is what every contender needs from them. (2) Business: both sell access to Trump’s circle to foreign clients (see the Srpska fees below), and that product loses value if Trump stops being the center (my reading).

Nov 7 nominee/faction consistency review: the older succession account describes Wiles’s chief-of-staff gatekeeping before the announced transition. Miller was named to succeed her, with the ledger reporting a Nov 9 handover and a political role for Wiles. White House gatekeeping and campaign-money control are separate channels; do not assume either disappears or transfers in full. No nominee endorsement is established. Evidence: mid-2026-11-06-miller-chief-staff.
